steps.label: ACCURACY MISLEADS ON IMBALANCE
steps.sub: Track ROC AUC instead -- ranks churners above loyal ones

code:
df = make_churn_data()
print(df.shape)                      # (2000, 6)
print(df.isna().sum()["monthly_charges"])  # 64 missing (~3%)
print(round(df.churned.mean(), 3))   # 0.344
caption: About 1 in 3 customers churns -- a meaningful imbalance.

code:
df.groupby("contract").churned.agg(["mean","size"])
# month-to-month: 0.462 (1094)
# one-year:       0.254 (493)
# two-year:       0.143 (413)

# churners avg 14.7mo tenure, 1.8 calls vs. stayers' 26.3mo, 1.4
caption: Patterns a model should pick up -- and a sanity check on its results later.

eyebrow: Split first, protect the test set
code:
X_tr, X_te, y_tr, y_te = train_test_split(X, y, test_size=0.2, stratify=y)
print(X_tr.shape, X_te.shape)         # (1600, 5) (400, 5)
print(y_tr.mean(), y_te.mean())       # 0.344  0.345
caption: From now on: all fitting, imputing, scaling uses X_tr only. Test stays sealed until Lesson 29.

eyebrow: The baseline: beat this or it wasn't worth it
code:
base = DummyClassifier(strategy="most_frequent").fit(X_tr, y_tr)
print(accuracy_score(y_te, base.predict(X_te)))        # 0.655
print(roc_auc_score(y_te, base.predict_proba(X_te)[:,1]))  # 0.5
caption: 0.655 "accuracy" is NOT impressive -- it's just predicting "stayed" for everyone.
Real output: month-to-month churns far more; churners cluster at short tenure.
